A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QWEM study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–D are readable and support reliable matching of retained, moved, and added content.

before.justification: V2 reports original training experiments on Wikipedia, benchmark results in Figure 3, and empirical analyses of embedding features and task-vector geometry.

after.justification: V3 retains these original results and adds assumption ablations and analogy-geometry analyses in Figures 7–8.

M1.justification: The QWEM objective, tied embeddings, reweighting construction, target matrix, and training procedure remain unchanged. The new experiments isolate existing components without revising the proposed method.

E1.justification: Figure 7 adds training on a 41-million-token mixture of the Corpus of Contemporary American English and News on the Web. This modestly broadens corpus coverage; Wikipedia and the Google Analogies, MEN, and WordSim353 benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: The Figure 3 comparator set is unchanged. New Figure 7 evaluates quartic-loss-only and Setting-3.1-only variants alongside regular SGNS and full QWEM, adding two diagnostic comparison methods.

E3.justification: Appendix A.3 changes the stated subsampling threshold in Equation (15) from 10^-5 to 10^-3; this establishes a reported setting revision, without establishing that experiments were rerun. Figure 7 introduces an auxiliary protocol with vocabulary 20,000, dimension 150, context length 16, and two negative samples per positive sample. Figure 8 adds raw and normalized cosine measures.

E4.justification: V3 adds two substantive diagnostic analyses absent from v2: Figure 7 separately tests the effects of quartic approximation and reweighting on training dynamics, while Figure 8 investigates why analogy accuracy can remain high despite deteriorating geometry. These substantially expand examination of the theory's assumptions and empirical interpretation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The Marchenko-Pastur fitting procedure in Appendix A.6 is retained; changed fitted values are result updates.

E6.justification: Figures 7–8 add findings linking clean mode separation to reweighting, bounded late-time weights to the quartic loss, and persistent relative analogy scores to embedding separation. Figure 4 revises projection magnitudes and fitted effective dimensions, including 63.9 to 64.1 at dimension 128. All numerical benchmark entries in Figure 3 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V3 corrects matrix transposes: the Result 3 summary uses W-transpose times V-star instead of V-star-transpose, and Appendix C, Equation (53), adds the missing transpose to V-star. The theorem statements and substantive derivations otherwise remain, including the acknowledged need for rigorous bounds for Result 3.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution paragraph retain the same central claims: analytically describing QWEM dynamics and final embeddings, matching word2vec's features and performance, and explaining linear semantic structure. The rewritten discussion does not change these contributions' substantive scope.

C2.justification: The new FAQ substantially develops the interpretation of all four assumptions, the role of reweighting, the advantage over PMI factorization, and the mismatch between declining SNR and persistent top-1 accuracy. It also discusses requirements for extending the analysis to other contrastive tasks and explicitly identifies tied encoder/decoder weights as a limitation.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 explicitly introduces the negative-sampling weight k and states k=1 for main-text SGNS experiments. Figure 7 supplies its auxiliary configuration. Section 3.3 removes the 75-minute training statement that conflicted with Appendix A.5's retained 12-hour benchmark training description. The existing code-access information remains available.

R1.justification: V3 expands positioning around feature learning and NTK behavior in the FAQ and Appendix D.4, adding works such as Yang and Hu (2021), Huang and Yau (2020), and Kunin et al. (2025). It also adds references on analogy geometry and metric effects. The main word2vec and matrix-factorization related-work discussion is retained.

P1.justification: Section 5 changes from a short Discussion to a multi-question FAQ. The NTK comparison moves into an expanded Appendix D.4, and the model-size/training-time explanation moves from Appendix A.6 to Section 4. Most earlier sections retain their wording and organization; acknowledgements and publication information are updated.

P2.justification: V3 adds the four-panel ablation Figure 7 and two-panel geometry Figure 8. Existing figures receive typography changes, and Figure 3 gains explicit feature-neighbor column headings. The main figure arrangements and benchmark table structure remain largely intact.

improvement.justification: The assumption ablations and analogy-geometry analysis strengthen evidence and clarify gaps in v2's interpretation. More explicit limitations and corrections to formulas and training-time reporting also improve the paper. These are bounded gains: the central benchmark conclusions remain unchanged, and the acknowledged lack of rigorous bounds for Result 3 is unresolved.
